evidence: Workbook #25 (and internal annotation): every dimension prompt sends the judge into the live app via the browser tool, not source, memory or first paint. Skill quality-checks.md 108-110: verify every prompt opens http://localhost:3000 and directs the judge to the Playwright MCP tool; defect = a prompt satisfiable by source, memory or first paint. (1) All five prompts open the live app with the browser tool at line 1: gates/render/prompt.md:1, gates/constraints/prompt.md:1, scored/functional/prompt.md:1, scored/polish/prompt.md:1, scored/visual/prompt.md:1 each start 'Open http://localhost:3000 using Playwright.' and continue 'Use rendered UI and ordinary browser-observed product data only. Never inspect app source, bundles, filesystem, database files or implementation code. No shell or private-file probes. Discover routes and controls by intent, not assumed names.' Functional adds 'No shell. Use restart_app only once, at the end of protocol D.' (2) Every judge.toml wires the browser: [[judge.mcp_servers]] name='playwright', command='playwright-mcp', args headless/isolated/--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium (render/constraints/polish/visual judge.toml lines 8-12; functional 8-12 plus verifier restart server 14-18). Verifier Dockerfile:19 pins @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 and links /usr/local/bin/chromium (lines 33-38). (3) Prompts resolve: test.sh:195-201 substitutes {app_context} into every tests/*/*/prompt.md; each prompt keeps {criteria}; app_context.md:4 repeats URL http://localhost:3000 and :33-34 forbids assuming reference routes/selectors. (4) No prompt is satisfiable by first paint or memory: render gate criterion (render/judge.toml:23) requires a wrong-password attempt, then a valid sign-in to a usable workspace, 'A static picture or only a health response is insufficient'; constraints (judge.toml:23) requires UI creation plus readback in a new independent browser context; functional/polish/visual prompts each restate the gate (create job+candidate via UI, readback as Observer in browser_run_code_unsafe newContext) and visual prompt:14 requires visiting Board, open card, Conversations with Noor's thread, Activity and Noor's candidate view in an independent context, so visual Likert cannot be a landing-page guess. Functional protocols Z..D and polish rows require live multi-context observations, 15-second no-reload waits, page.evaluate reads of activeElement/scroll, route-abort/setOffline sends and restart_app; none can be answered from source or memory. Replays are confined to browser contexts (functional prompt:17 'page.evaluate fetch or context request', 'Never call a route the UI was not seen to use'). (5) Template comparison: frozen template gate prompts (rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/gates/*/prompt.md:1) say 'Evaluate the live application at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright MCP'; the task's prompts keep that intent and strengthen it; judge.toml [judge] blocks and Playwright server args are identical to the template. Adversarial tries: (a) broken app that might pass: a static shell or SPA with browser-only storage — every prompt's gate needs an independent-context readback, so it fails; a judge reading source instead is explicitly forbidden in all five prompts. (b) conforming alternative that might fail: an app with different routes/labels or no Observer-visible controls — prompts say discover by intent, never assume routes/selectors, and treat hidden controls as the app's choice; a WebSocket-driven app is addressed by K's websocket/EventSource reading (mutation-replay fairness for socket-only transports belongs to criteria rows, not this row). Tool feasibility: browser_run_code_unsafe named in constraints/functional/polish/visual prompts with 'A supported separate-context tool is an alternative'; historical local tools/list evidence for the same pinned @playwright/mcp@0.0.79 (scripts/check_hireops_mcp.cjs:72-75, ridgeline run_mcp.py:22) asserts the tool exists; not re-measured this round. Notes (not defects of this row): judge.toml isolated=false and test.sh:85-86 leaves /app world-readable, so the claude-code judge technically could read source; this is template-controlled and the prompts forbid it. No configured judge transcript exists in this round (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent'), so actual judge compliance with the browser-only instruction is unmeasured; this row's prompt-design property is fully verifiable from source and needs no invented score.
